title: Production Go: Config, Logging, and Graceful Shutdown

questions.prompt: Where should a production service get its configuration?

options.text: From flags and environment variables, not hardcoded
Hardcoded in the source and recompiled to change it
From a random number generator
Only from command-line flags, never environment

questions.explanation: Config (and secrets) should come from flags and environment so behavior changes per environment without recompiling; env suits deploy config, flags suit local overrides.

questions.prompt: What does the standard `log/slog` package provide, and since when?

options.text: Structured (key/value) logging, in the standard library since Go 1.21
A web framework since Go 1.0
A testing library
A replacement for fmt.Println only

questions.explanation: log/slog (Go 1.21+) emits structured logs as key/value pairs, which log systems can index and query.

questions.prompt: What does http.Server.Shutdown(ctx) do that Close does not?

options.text: It stops accepting new connections and lets in-flight requests finish (up to the deadline)
It restarts the server
It deletes all logs
Nothing — they are identical

questions.explanation: Shutdown drains active requests gracefully within the context deadline; Close terminates connections abruptly.

questions.prompt: You turn SIGINT/SIGTERM into a cancellable context with signal.____.
questions.explanation: signal.NotifyContext returns a context that is cancelled when one of the given signals arrives, so you can wait on ctx.Done() to begin shutdown.

questions.prompt: Why must you ignore http.ErrServerClosed from ListenAndServe?

options.text: It's the normal result of a graceful shutdown, not a failure
It never actually occurs
It means the port is in use
It indicates a panic

questions.explanation: A graceful Shutdown causes ListenAndServe to return http.ErrServerClosed; treating it as fatal makes every clean shutdown look like a crash.

questions.prompt: Which are good production practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give Shutdown a bounded timeout so it can't hang forever
Expose a cheap health-check endpoint for probes
Log as JSON in production with log/slog
Print unstructured text logs for machine querying

questions.explanation: Bounded shutdown, a lightweight health check, and structured JSON logs are all good practice; unstructured text is hard for tools to query.
